# `nodes`

Group: **Nodes**. Which hardware the on-board units run on.

8 settings. The status column says whether editing a setting changes a run; see [how to read these tables](../overview.md). Paths use `[]` for a list element and `*` for a map key.

## General

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-nodes-default-obu"></span>`nodes.default_obu` | string | | `obu/unex-obu-301-craton2` | `obu/cohda-mk5`, `obu/cohda-mk6c-qualcomm-9150`, `obu/generic-automotive-soc-no-hsm`, `obu/pq-capable-hypothetical`, `obu/unex-obu-301-craton2`, `obu/unex-obu-301-craton2-software`<br>recommended A shipped automotive profile; a post-quantum signature needs one with figures for it. | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The profile every equipped vehicle uses unless its class overrides it. The on-board unit hardware vehicles carry. It decides how long signing and verifying a message take. Model slot: family `hardware-profile`, see [model parameters](models.md). |
| <span id="s-nodes-compute-tier"></span>`nodes.compute_tier` | string | | `medium` | `abstract`, `medium`, `high` | advanced | :material-circle-half-full:{ title="Partly active" } `partial` | The compute tier. *Status: abstract: signing and verification cost a microsecond and no node is ever compute-bound. medium: every operation costs the hardware profile's service time and queues FIFO behind one CPU server and the profile's HSM. high: the CPU runs as the profile's cores, so software cryptography and application tasks are served in parallel; it changes nothing for a profile whose cryptography runs on its HSM. Processor sharing, priority classes and HSM latency distributions are not built.* |
| <span id="s-nodes-backend-tier"></span>`nodes.backend_tier` | string | | `medium` | `abstract`, `medium`, `high` | advanced | :material-circle-half-full:{ title="Partly active" } `partial` | The backend tier. *Status: abstract: backend entities never queue (64 servers, no fixed overhead). medium and high: each entity is an M/M/c with the deployment's servers and overhead, and the RA shuffles; high adds nothing over medium yet.* |
| <span id="s-nodes-verify-queue-depth"></span>`nodes.verify_queue_depth` | integer | messages | | [1, 4096]<br>recommended 16 to 256; 64 is one second of 6 neighbours at 10 Hz. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How many received messages wait for signature verification before new ones are dropped, per node. 64 unless set (no profile publishes a depth). How many received messages can wait for signature verification; when the processor falls behind, messages beyond it are dropped. |
| <span id="s-nodes-peer-cert-cache"></span>`nodes.peer_cert_cache` | integer | certificates | | [1, 65536]<br>recommended 128 (engine default; no device publishes one); 16 to 1024. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How many peer certificates each vehicle or roadside unit holds before it forgets the least recently used one. 128 unless set (no profile publishes one). How many other stations' certificates each vehicle or roadside radio unit remembers; when it forgets one, that vehicle's next short-form message cannot be checked until its certificate is requested again. |
| <span id="s-nodes-validated-cert-cache"></span>`nodes.validated_cert_cache` | integer | certificates | `4096` | [1, 1048576]<br>recommended 4,096 (engine default; no device publishes one); 16 to 65,536. The peer certificate cache (128) usually forgets first. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How many validated end-entity certificates each device remembers, so a repeat signer costs only its signature check (least recently used evicted first). 4,096 unless set (`v2xw_node::rxval::EE_CACHE`; no device publishes one). The peer certificate cache usually bounds it first. How many already-checked certificates of other vehicles each device remembers, so a known sender costs only its signature check; a forgotten one is checked from scratch the next time it is heard. A small cache is what a certificate-flooding attack exhausts. |
| <span id="s-nodes-hsm-sign-lower-us"></span>`nodes.hsm_sign_lower_us` | number | us | | (0, 1000000]<br>recommended Unset (every signature at the CRATON2's published &lt;9 ms bound; no typical value is published); 613 us (software ECDSA P-256 on a Cortex-A53: `openssl speed` on a Raspberry Pi 3B, community benchmark) to 9,000 us. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The lower edge of the HSM signing time, microseconds, for a profile that publishes only an upper bound (the CRATON2's "&lt;9 ms"). Set, each signature takes a time drawn uniformly between this edge and the bound from the node's own random stream; unset, every signature takes the bound itself (the worst case). No typical value is published for the CRATON2/SECTON eHSM (searched 2026-10-13: Unex sheets, Autotalks pages, CMVP #3556/#4395 policies), so the default stays the bound. The fastest a hardware security module signs a message, when its maker only publishes a worst case; each signature then takes a random time between this and the worst case instead of always the worst case. |

## Choices

The labelled values of every closed or model setting above.

??? note "`nodes.default_obu`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `obu/cohda-mk5` | Cohda mk5 (cannot sign) | Its sources publish no ECDSA signing rate, so a vehicle on it could not sign a message; choose a unit that publishes one. |
 | `obu/cohda-mk6c-qualcomm-9150` | Cohda mk6c qualcomm 9150 | Commercial C-V2X OBU (Cohda MK6C EVK: Qualcomm 9150 PC5 modem, NXP i.MX 8QXP host, NXP SXF1800 secure element). |
 | `obu/generic-automotive-soc-no-hsm` | Generic automotive soc no hsm | Generic automotive SoC with no secure element or accelerator: the profile for scenarios asking what happens when all crypto runs in software. |
 | `obu/pq-capable-hypothetical` | Pq capable hypothetical (cannot sign) | Its sources publish no ECDSA signing rate, so a vehicle on it could not sign a message; choose a unit that publishes one. |
 | `obu/unex-obu-301-craton2` | Unex OBU 301 craton2 | Reference OBU profile (Autotalks CRATON2 in the Unex OBU-301E). |
 | `obu/unex-obu-301-craton2-software` | Unex OBU 301 craton2 software | The reference OBU (Unex OBU-301E, Autotalks CRATON2) with its security hardware set aside: every ECDSA operation runs in software on the application cores. |

??? note "`nodes.compute_tier`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `abstract` | Fast (abstract) | Closed-form stand-ins: cheapest, for very large fleets; least faithful. |
 | `medium` | Standard (medium) | The models the literature agrees on, without frame-level detail. The usual choice. |
 | `high` | Detailed (high) | Frame-level or geometry-traced detail: the most faithful and the slowest. |

??? note "`nodes.backend_tier`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `abstract` | Fast (abstract) | Closed-form stand-ins: cheapest, for very large fleets; least faithful. |
 | `medium` | Standard (medium) | The models the literature agrees on, without frame-level detail. The usual choice. |
 | `high` | Detailed (high) | Frame-level or geometry-traced detail: the most faithful and the slowest. |
